messages.content:
You are a helpful writing assistant. You help professionals draft clear,
effective workplace communication.

I have to tell my manager I'm going to miss the Friday deadline on the
migration. It's my fault - I underestimated it. I want to say it straight
without it turning into a whole thing. Can you help me word it?

Here’s a clear, professional draft that owns the misstep, gives a concrete path forward, and keeps the tone calm and solution-focused:

**Subject:** Update on migration timeline  

Hi [Manager's Name],  

I need to update you on the migration: I won’t be able to meet the Friday deadline. I underestimated the complexity of a few components, and it’s going to take longer than planned.  

I’m on track to complete it by [new date/time]. To keep impact minimal, I’ve [briefly note what you’re doing: prioritized core functionality / scheduled focused work through Thursday / looped in X to review, etc.]. I can share a quick status breakdown today and discuss any adjustments needed on our end.  

I take full responsibility for the scoping misstep, and I’ll make sure we’re more precise with estimates on the next phase. Let me know the best time to connect.  

Thanks,  
[Your Name]  

**Why this works:**  
- Opens with the hard news so there’s no ambiguity  
- Acknowledges responsibility in one clean sentence (no over-apologizing or deflection)  
- Pivots immediately to a new timeline and mitigation steps  
- Closes with accountability + openness to discuss, which signals maturity  

**If you're sending this over Slack/Teams:**  
You can trim it to:  
> Hi [Name], I need to update you on the migration—I won’t hit the Friday deadline. I underestimated a few components and need until [new date] to wrap it up. I’m [mitigation step] to keep impact low and can share a status breakdown today. I own the scoping misstep and will tighten estimates moving forward. Let me know when you have 10 to align on next steps.  

**Quick tips for delivery:**  
- Send it as early as you know you’ll miss the deadline—early notice shows respect for their planning time.  
- Keep the conversation focused on the new timeline and mitigation; if they ask why, give the straightforward “underestimated complexity” explanation once, then pivot to next steps.  
- Avoid phrases like “I’m so sorry” or “I really messed up.” They can trigger unnecessary escalation. Own it once, clearly, then show control.  

Want me to adjust the tone or fill in the new date/mitigation details with your specifics?
